meter_watch_note: Continuous polls such as {tool} are free, which is why the two numbers differ.
error_network: Could not reach the server. Check your connection.
error_repo_unresolved: That repository could not be resolved. Check the slug or remote against what is registered.
error_repo_slug_taken: That repository name is already in use.
error_remote_taken: That remote is already registered to another repository.
error_wrong_status: The job is not in a state that allows this.
error_already_claimed: Another agent has already claimed that job.
error_ticket_already_linked: That ticket is already linked to an open job.
error_dependency_cycle: That would make the jobs depend on each other in a circle.
error_lease_held: Another agent holds the lease on that repository. It will expire.
error_lease_not_held: You do not hold the lease on that repository.
error_team_slug_taken: That team name is already in use.
error_team_in_use: That team still has repositories assigned to it.
error_not_a_member: That account is not a member of this organization.
error_already_a_member: That account is already a member.
error_invite_invalid: That invitation is not valid. It may have been used already, or expired.
error_invite_wrong_account: That invitation was issued to a different address. Sign in as the invited account.
error_internal: Something went wrong on the server. Try again shortly.
error_forbidden: Your role does not allow that.
error_invalid_credentials: That did not work. Try again.
error_ceremony_expired: That took too long. Start again.
error_credential_already_registered: That authenticator is already registered to this account.
error_unknown_credential: That passkey is not registered here. Try a different one.
error_last_passkey: This is the only passkey on the account. Add another before removing this one.
error_last_owner: An organization has to keep at least one owner.
error_credential_expired: That code has expired or has already been used.
error_wrong_audience: That token was issued for a different service.
error_sso_required: This organization requires signing in through its identity provider.
error_rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
error_invalid_client: That application is not registered here.
error_invalid_grant: That authorization is no longer valid. Start the connection again.
error_unsupported_grant_type: This server does not support that way of getting a token.
error_invalid_scope: That set of permissions is not one this server issues.
error_tracker_unreachable: The issue tracker could not be reached. Try again shortly.
error_passkey_cancelled: No passkey was used. Try again when you are ready.
error_passkey_already_registered: That authenticator is already registered to this account.
error_passkey_misconfigured: This site is not configured correctly for passkeys. Tell whoever runs it that the relying party ID does not match this origin.
error_session_resolve_failed: Something went wrong resolving your session.
copy_clipboard_refused: The browser refused clipboard access. Select the text above and copy it by hand.
client_note_claude_code: Then run `claude mcp login otto-factory` in an interactive terminal to consent — a `-p` session cannot open a browser and will report the server as unauthenticated.
client_note_copilot: Copilot only offers the browser consent from its interactive session; a `-p` run with no credential reports no such tool rather than asking. Script it with a token.
client_note_generic: Streamable HTTP. A conforming client needs nothing but this URL: the 401 it gets back points at the protected-resource document, which points at the authorization server.
login_passkey_hint: Your passkey knows who you are — there is nothing to type.
login_unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys. Try a current version of Safari, Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
login_recovery_hint: Lost every device you registered? There is no email to recover through, so an admin of an organization you belong to can issue you a one-time code to register a new passkey.
login_recovery_link: If you have one, use it here.
signup_intro: No password, and no email to confirm. You create a passkey now, and that is how you sign in from then on.
signup_unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys. Try a current version of Safari, Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
signup_platform_hint: Your device will ask for your fingerprint, face, or screen lock. A security key or your phone works too.
signup_no_platform_hint: You will need a security key or your phone — this device has no built-in authenticator.
signup_ready_intro: Tell us how to address you. Your email is how colleagues invite you to an organization — we never send anything to it.
signup_email_hint: Your unique identifier here. Nothing is ever sent to it.
signup_name_hint: Optional. Shown to the other people in your organizations.
signup_second_passkey_link: Next, add a second passkey from your settings.
signup_second_passkey_hint: One passkey is one device, and there is no email to recover through if you lose it.
claim_intro: Use the one-time code an admin gave you. It works once and replaces every passkey the account had.
invite_missing_token: This link is missing its token. Ask whoever invited you to send another.
invite_no_email: an account with no email set
invite_only_invited_address: An invitation can only be accepted by the address it was sent to.
invite_wrong_account_hint: Sign out and sign in as the invited address, then open this link again.
invite_error_fallback: That invitation could not be accepted.
orgnew_intro_first: Everything in otto-factory belongs to an organization — repos, the queue, your agents' tokens. Create one to get started.
orgnew_slug_hint: Appears in URLs and in every agent's configuration. It cannot be changed later.
settings_subtitle: Your passkeys and how you are addressed.
settings_one_passkey_warning: You have one passkey, which means one device. We send no email, so if you lose it the only way back in is an admin of an organization you belong to — and if you are the only owner of yours, there is none. Add a second.
settings_passkeys_description: Each one signs you in on its own. Add your phone as well as this device.
settings_profile_description: Your email is an identifier here. Nothing is sent to it.
settings_email_hint: How colleagues invite you to an organization.
billing_no_org_title: You are not in an organization yet.
trackercb_no_pending_state: This connect flow did not start in this tab, or it has already been completed. Open your organization’s Trackers page and start it again.
trackercb_github_no_code: GitHub sent no authorization code. The App must have "Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation" enabled before an installation can be verified.
trackercb_no_code: The provider sent no authorization code. Start the connect flow again.
trackercb_error_fallback: Could not finish connecting that tracker.
settings_language_description: Applies everywhere you sign in, not just this browser.
orgnav_missing_body: Nothing here is called {slug}. Check the address, or pick one from the bar above.
overview_refresh_failed: Refresh failed. {reason} Showing the result from {age}.
overview_paused: Updates paused while you were away. Interact with the page to resume.

match.countPlural=one: # pending job is waiting on a dependency and cannot be claimed yet.
match.countPlural=other: # pending jobs are waiting on a dependency and cannot be claimed yet.

overview_blocked_also_pending: They are counted under {status} as well.
overview_empty_hint: Jobs are created by agents over MCP.
overview_period_description: Metered tool calls against the plan.
overview_repos_empty_hint: A job has to belong to one, so nothing can be queued until a repo exists.
queue_read_only_note: Read-only. Jobs are queued and completed by agents over MCP.
queue_empty_hint: Jobs are created by agents over MCP.
queue_showing_capped: Only the most recent {limit} are shown.
job_missing_body: Nothing in {org} is called {id}. Job ids are counted per organization, so the same id in another org is a different job.
job_waiting_on_description: This job cannot be claimed until all of these are completed.
job_metadata_description: Opaque to otto-factory — whatever the queueing skill put here.
usage_subtitle: The billable unit is one MCP tool call.
usage_out_enforced: This organization is out of its included operations and billable tools are being refused. Reads keep working — the queue stays visible, and nothing already queued is lost.
usage_out_not_enforced: This organization is past its included operations. Nothing is being refused yet.
usage_warning: Most of this period's included operations have been used.
usage_why_body: Every call is recorded, but not every call is billed. {tool} is a continuous long poll — an agent waiting for work holds one open more or less permanently — and charging it flat would bill an idle agent tens of thousands of calls a month for doing nothing. Reads that answer “what is going on”, including this page, are free too.
usage_why_history: The full history is kept regardless of how a call was classified, so a change to what counts can be applied without losing what happened.
audit_subtitle: Who did what in {org}. Admins only.
audit_error_load: Could not read the audit log.
teams_subtitle: A team scopes repos and their queues. A repo with no team is visible to the whole org.
teams_empty_body: Teams are optional. Without one, every repo is visible to every member.
teams_roster_empty: Nobody is on this team yet.
trackers_subtitle: Connect an issue tracker once per organization, then point individual repos at a project on the {link} page. A labelled issue becomes a job; finishing the job writes back a comment and moves the ticket.
trackers_admin_only: Only an owner or admin can connect a tracker.
trackers_disconnect_note: Disconnecting leaves each repo's binding in place but inert — nothing syncs until {provider} is connected again.
trackers_not_connected_github: Not connected. You will install the otto-factory GitHub App on the organization whose issues this org works from, and come back here.
trackers_not_connected_jira: Not connected. You will authorize otto-factory against one Atlassian site. Grant access to a single site — one JIRA site per organization is what this stores.
trackers_not_configured: This deployment does not offer {provider} sync. An operator configures it with the {credentials} credentials.
repos_subtitle: Every job belongs to one of these. An agent that cannot resolve its checkout to a registered repo gets an error naming these slugs, never a guess.
repos_field_slug_hint: What agents will type. It cannot be changed later.
repos_field_remotes_hint: One per line, in any form git prints. SSH and HTTPS spellings of one repository collapse to a single row.
repos_field_team_hint: Leave org-wide unless this repo should only be visible to one team.
repos_empty_admin: Register one above, or let an agent do it with the {tool} tool.
repos_empty_member: Ask an owner or admin to register one.
repos_leases_failed: Could not read the leases on this repo.
repos_no_leases: Nobody holds a lease on {repo} right now.
repos_leases_note: Leases are advisory. The server cannot see a git push, so a lease makes a collision visible — it does not prevent one.
repos_bindings_failed: Could not read this repo's tracker bindings.
repos_binding_inactive: Stored, but nothing syncs until {provider} is connected on the {link} page.
repos_bindings_note: An issue in the bound project carrying the trigger label becomes a job in this repo. GitHub takes {githubRef}; JIRA takes a project key. Both are matched exactly against what the provider sends.
members_subtitle: Everyone who can sign in to {org}.
members_claim_headline: Passkeys cleared. Give them this code —
members_claim_caveat: it is shown only now and cannot be looked up again. If you lose it, reset again.
members_claim_note: It works once, expires in 14 days, and is the only way back into that account. Anyone holding it can register a passkey on it, so hand it over the way you would a password.
members_invite_description: A single-use code, good for 14 days. You deliver it — nothing is emailed.
members_invite_minted_headline: Invitation for {email}. Send them one of these —
members_invite_minted_caveat: it is shown only now, and cannot be looked up again. If you lose it, invite them again.
members_invite_minted_note: Only an account signed in as {email} can redeem it, so a code that goes astray is not a free seat.
members_force_logout_title: End every browser session this account holds. Leaves their tokens alone.
members_reset_title: Clear their passkeys and get a one-time code they can use to register a new one. Ends their sessions.
members_reset_confirm: Clear every passkey for {who}? They will be signed out everywhere and must register again with the code you are about to be given.
members_roster_note: Removing someone also clears their team memberships and revokes the tokens they held in this org — their agents stop on their next call.
members_invites_empty: Nobody is waiting on an invitation.
connect_subtitle: Any client that speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP works. Nothing here depends on a particular agent's plugins, hooks, or skills.
connect_no_endpoint: The server did not report an MCP endpoint. Its {document} document is what this page reads.
connect_endpoint_note: Tokens are audienced for exactly this URI. A token minted here is refused anywhere else, and its organization — {org} — is fixed when it is issued and cannot be changed.
connect_token_placeholder_note: Replace the placeholder with a token — mint one below. The token is shown once.
connect_oauth_note: The client registers itself and sends you here to approve it. Nothing is pasted, and you can revoke it from this page afterwards.
connect_new_token_warning: This is shown once. Only a SHA-256 hash of it is stored, so nobody — including us — can show it to you again.
connect_pat_description: The compatibility path, for clients whose OAuth support is partial.
connect_field_name_hint: Shown in the list below. It is all you will have to go on when deciding what to revoke.
connect_scopes_note: You can only grant scopes you hold. {scope} needs an owner or admin of this organization.
connect_live_note: Yours only, OAuth grants included. Revoking one stops that agent on its next call, not at some later expiry.
connect_error_metadata: Could not read the server configuration.
